At other places,
PW1 also denied that no dowry was demanded by the accused and that her daughter and the accused were living happily before her death, but all these general statements are not sufficient enough to assemble the charges against the accused Sanjay Rathore for offence under section 498A/306 IPC, more so, in light of the fact that on specific circumstances which were sup- plied by him to the police in his earlier statement Ex.
PW1/PX1, PW1 has recanted and failed to narrate specific incidents of cru- elty or harassment to his deceased daughter and abetting of her suicide by the accused.
He went on to assert having not given any statement before the police in relation to the present case.

There- fore, it is held that the prosecution has failed to establish points for determination no.2 and 3 as noted above, and consequently, the charges for offence under section 498A/306 IPC against the accused falls face down.
23.
The testimonies of rest of the witnesses are formal in nature which are not sufficient to place the gauntlet of guilt on the accused.
Thus, accused Sanjay Rathore stand acquitted of the Pg No. 15 of 16 State Vs. Sanjay Rathore SC no. 492/2019 FIR no.780/18 PS Mehrauli charges framed against him.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Points for determination (1) Whether Smt. Renu, wife of the accused, died on account of suicide by consuming poisonous substance on 14.07.2017.
(2) Whether Smt. Renu was subjected to cruelty or harassment by the accused Sanjay Rathore with a view to coercing her or her family members to meet any unlawful demand of any property or valuable security/dowry demand.
(3) Whether accused had instigated the commission of the suicide by the said Smt. Renu.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
14. In so far as the first point for determination is con- cerned, as such, there has been no expostulation on behalf of the accused.
Accused has avouched in his statement under section 313 Cr.P.C that his wife consumed poison in a fit of rage.
There- fore, it is held that the prosecution has failed to establish points for determination no.2 and 3 as noted above, and consequently, the charges for offence under section 498A/306 IPC against the accused falls face down.
23.
The testimonies of rest of the witnesses are formal in nature which are not sufficient to place the gauntlet of guilt on the accused.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, accused Sanjay Rathore stand acquitted of the Pg No. 15 of 16 State Vs. Sanjay Rathore SC no. 492/2019 FIR no.780/18 PS Mehrauli charges framed against him.
He is set at liberty.
